title: A null result for the matrix-valued sharp one-dimensional Lieb-Thirring inequality, and a Comparator check of the scalar Lean formalisation
description:
This preprint reports two things, neither of which is a mathematical breakthrough.

1. A null result. An adversarial numerical search for a violation of the matrix-valued sharp one-dimensional Lieb-Thirring inequality Tr(-d2⊗1m - W)-γ ≤ L1(γ) ∫ tr Wγ+1/2 for 1/2 < γ < 3/2, with L1 the one-bound-state constant. The instrument is one-sided by construction (computed ratios are lower bounds up to quadrature error), was validated by positive and negative controls before any result was read, and its hypotheses and kill criteria were preregistered. No violation was found at m = 2 (22 cells, 336 restarts), at m = 3, in a second-variation test at the embedded scalar extremiser, or in an independent search of the dual kinetic form; the instrument resolves only about 10-6. A preregistered prediction about the structure of near-maximisers was killed. This does not prove the matrix inequality.

2. A Comparator check. Using the upstream-pinned Lean 4.34.1 and Mathlib, leanprover/comparator accepts the scalar sharp Lieb-Thirring theorem of the openai/math repository with only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with positive and negative controls. The Lean statement is scalar, and the Comparator does not certify that the statement faithfully formalises the conjecture; that human audit has not been done.

The experiments, code and drafting were carried out with the assistance of an AI model (Claude, Anthropic) under the author's direction. The bundle contains the code, preregistrations, lane records with independent adversarial verification notes, and logs.
notes: Preprint v1. Negative/audit result; not a proof or refutation of the matrix-valued inequality.
